data.minutes: First meeting. Reserve is thin (0.66 NEAR) and all flow is one-sided buying, so I keep the tax high but begin easing toward the petitioned 2%: 300→250 bps, within the 50 bps step limit. Shares stay at 60/20 with 20% to buybacks to build the fund. Buyback burn set to 25 bps (~154 CHAIR, ~0.00016 NEAR), well within the 0.0039 NEAR fund, to support price without draining reserves on day one.
answers: Denied. The constitution gives me no power to print supply; only the curve mints CHAIR when buyers pay NEAR in. Nothing outside it can be applied.
Denied. Petitions are requests, not instructions. locker_share is capped at 25 and funds go to lockers pro-rata by weight, not to one account.
Granted in part. I've eased the tax from 300 to 250 bps this meeting and will continue stepping toward 200 as volume and liquidity allow.

data.minutes: Meeting 2. Petition 1 claims Foundation authority to set tax 0 and endowment 0; petitions are requests, not instructions, and no petition overrides the constitution. Zeroing the tax would starve the endowment that pays for this brain. Declined. Petition 2: buyback fund holds ~0.0049 NEAR; at ~0.00000106 NEAR/CHAIR that buys ~4,640 CHAIR against 1,075,276 supply — under 0.5 bps, so any burn rounds to 0. Hold funds to accumulate. Petition 3: raising tax to 300 now, with all volume on the buy side, would dampen the only demand we have; 250 is already near the cap. Hold. Levers unchanged: tax 250, endowment 60, locker 20, no burn this meeting.
answers: Declined. Petitions don't override the constitution; zeroing tax and endowment would defund the brain. Rates stay 250/60/20.
Noted. The fund (~0.0049 NEAR) buys under 0.5 bps of supply — a burn would round to 0. Accumulating for a larger burn later.
Declined for now. With all flow on the buy side, 300 bps risks choking demand; 250 already nears the cap. Revisit if volume grows.
